context.summary: Refactor the ECS module (src/engine/ecs/) to serve as the runtime foundation for a 3D web game engine built on Three.js WebGPU renderer with TSL (Three.js Shading Language). The current ECS has solid type safety, schema-based component definitions, change tracking, and JSON serialization, but has correctness bugs, performance issues, and missing features required for a real-time 3D engine.
context.codebase: TypeScript project using Vite, React, pnpm. The ECS lives in src/engine/ecs/ with files: types.ts (interfaces), entity.ts (EntityManager with generation-based IDs), storage.ts (SparseSetStore), world.ts (EcsWorld implementation), systems.ts (Scheduler), bridge.ts (JSON serialization). Supporting modules: src/engine/schema.ts (schema builder + defaults), src/engine/validate.ts, src/engine/materialize.ts, src/engine/codec.ts.
key_patterns: Component registry is a Record<string, SchemaLike> — generics propagate types to queries
Entity IDs encode generation * 1_000_000 + index for stale-reference safety
SparseSetStore uses dense arrays for iteration + Map<EntityId, number> for sparse lookup
Change tracking per component type: added/removed/updated Sets cleared on beginFrame/endFrame
World interface in types.ts, implementation in EcsWorld class in world.ts
Scheduler is a flat array of (world, dt) => void system functions

execution_workflow.description: Each task is executed sequentially by Claude in a bash loop. For each task, Claude must: (1) read the relevant files, (2) implement the changes described, (3) write or update tests, (4) run typecheck and tests to validate. A task is only marked done when both typecheck and all tests pass.
rules: Never skip validation — both typecheck and tests must pass before marking done
If an existing test breaks, determine if the test expectation needs updating (because behavior intentionally changed) or if the implementation is wrong
Each task must be self-contained: do not leave partial changes that break the build
Preserve all existing public API signatures unless the task explicitly says to change them
Add tests for every new public method or behavior change
Keep the ecs/index.ts barrel export up to date when adding new files
After a task passes validation confidently (typecheck + tests), commit the changes with a concise message (e.g., 'ecs: fix destroyEntity listener ordering') and mark done

tasks.title: Fix destroyEntity listener ordering
tasks.description: In src/engine/ecs/world.ts, the destroyEntity method currently: (1) removes all components from stores, (2) marks the entity dead in EntityManager, (3) fires destroy listeners. This means listeners receive a stale entity ID with no accessible components — they can't do cleanup that requires reading component data (e.g., disposing Three.js objects based on a MeshComponent). Fix the ordering so listeners fire FIRST while the entity is still alive and components are still accessible, THEN remove components from stores and record removals in change tracking, THEN mark dead in entity manager. Update any existing tests in ecs/world.test.ts that assert on the current ordering. Add a new test that verifies a destroy listener can call world.getComponent() and world.hasComponent() on the entity being destroyed and get valid results.
success_criteria: destroyEntity fires listeners before removing components and before marking entity dead
A destroy listener can call getComponent/hasComponent on the entity and get valid results
Change tracking still records removals correctly for destroyed entity components
All existing tests pass (updated if they asserted on old ordering)
pnpm typecheck passes
pnpm test:run passes

tasks.title: Query iteration safety during mutation
tasks.description: In src/engine/ecs/world.ts, the query() method's iterator uses baseStore.entities() which returns the LIVE backing array of the SparseSetStore. If a system destroys an entity or removes a component during iteration, the sparse set's swap-remove can skip entities (the last element is moved into the removed slot, and the for-of loop advances past it). Fix by snapshotting the base entity array at the start of iteration: replace `const baseEntities = baseStore.entities()` with `const baseEntities = baseStore.entities().slice()`. Also snapshot the entity list in the include-length-0 branch (line 173: `Array.from(world.entities())` is already a copy, so that branch is safe). Add a test that proves correctness: create 3 entities with a component, iterate a query, destroy the first entity during iteration, and verify all 3 entities were visited (or at minimum, no entity was silently skipped). The existing `if (!baseStore.has(entity))` guard at line 211 should remain as a secondary safety check for entities that were destroyed during iteration.
success_criteria: Query iterator snapshots the base entity array so swap-remove during iteration cannot skip entities
Test proves that destroying an entity during query iteration does not skip other entities
The has() guard remains as a secondary check for destroyed-during-iteration entities
All existing query tests still pass
pnpm typecheck passes
pnpm test:run passes

tasks.title: EntityManager.reserve() free-list performance
tasks.description: In src/engine/ecs/entity.ts, the reserve() method uses this.free.indexOf(index) (O(n) scan) and this.free.splice(freeIndex, 1) (O(n) shift) to remove an index from the free list. Loading a saved world with 10K entities means O(n^2) total cost. Fix by changing the free list from an array to a Set<number>. The Set gives O(1) has/delete for reserve(). For create(), which currently does this.free.pop() to grab a reusable index, use Set.values().next().value to grab an arbitrary element, then delete it. Alternatively, maintain both a Set (for reserve lookups) and push the same values — but the simplest approach is a Set-only free list. Update the destroy() method which currently does this.free.push(index) to use Set.add(). Make sure all existing entity.test.ts tests pass. Add a test that reserves 100 entities by ID and verifies they're all alive and have correct IDs.
success_criteria: Free list is a Set<number> instead of number[]
reserve() uses Set.delete() instead of indexOf + splice — O(1) instead of O(n)
create() grabs a reusable index from the Set in O(1)
destroy() adds to the Set
All existing entity tests pass
New test verifies bulk reserve of 100 entities works correctly
pnpm typecheck passes
pnpm test:run passes

tasks.title: In-place component mutation with dirty tracking (getMut)
tasks.description: Add a getMut<K>(entity, type) method to the World interface and EcsWorld class. getMut returns the direct reference to the stored component object (same as getComponent) but ALSO marks the component as updated in the change tracker by calling recordUpdated(type, entity). This lets systems mutate component data in-place without allocating a new object. If the entity is not alive or doesn't have the component, return undefined (same as getComponent). getMut must NOT record an update if the component was added in the current frame (same logic as recordUpdated — if it's in the added set, it stays as added, not updated). Add to: (1) World interface in types.ts, (2) EcsWorld class in world.ts. Add tests: (a) getMut returns the same reference as getComponent, (b) mutating the returned object is visible via getComponent, (c) getMut marks the component as updated in change tracking, (d) getMut on a component added in the same frame does not double-record as both added and updated, (e) getMut returns undefined for dead entities and missing components.

EcsWorld.getMut returns the stored reference and calls recordUpdated
Mutating the reference is visible via getComponent (proves same reference)

tasks.title: Tag / marker components

2. src/engine/validate.ts: Add validation case for 'tag' type — accepts true, undefined, or any value (tags are presence-only so validation is lenient). Or simply: value must be exactly `true`.

4. src/engine/ecs/types.ts: Update ComponentData so that when the schema is a TagSchema, the data type is `true`. 5. src/engine/ecs/world.ts: In addComponent, if the registry schema for the type has type === 'tag', store `true` as the value regardless of what data was passed. tasks.title: SparseSetStore: replace Map with flat array
tasks.description:
In src/engine/ecs/storage.ts, replace the Map<EntityId, number> sparse index with a flat array indexed by entity index (extracted via getEntityIndex from entity.ts). This gives true O(1) lookup without hash overhead.

Changes to SparseSetStore:
- Import getEntityIndex from ./entity
- Replace `private readonly sparse = new Map<EntityId, number>()` with `private readonly sparse: (number | undefined)[] = []`
- has(entity): extract index via getEntityIndex(entity), check sparse[index] !== undefined AND denseEntities[sparse[index]] === entity (the second check prevents stale generation matches)
- get(entity): same pattern — extract index, check sparse, verify entity match in dense
- set(entity): extract index, check sparse[index] and denseEntities match for existing, otherwise append to dense and set sparse[index]
- remove(entity): extract index, verify match, do swap-remove, update sparse for swapped entity, set sparse[index] = undefined (not delete)
- clear(): reset sparse to empty array (or fill with undefined), clear dense arrays

The entity in the dense array is the FULL entity ID (with generation). The sparse array maps entity INDEX (without generation) to dense position. The generation check happens by comparing denseEntities[sparsePos] === entity.

All existing storage.test.ts tests must pass. Add a test that verifies stale entity IDs (same index, different generation) do not collide — i.e., store.set(entity_gen0, value), after gen0 is destroyed and gen1 is created at the same index, store.has(entity_gen0) returns false.
success_criteria: SparseSetStore uses a flat array instead of Map for sparse index
has/get/set/remove use getEntityIndex to extract the array position
Stale generation IDs do not produce false positives (verified by dense entity check)
All existing storage tests pass
New test verifies generational safety (stale ID does not match)
pnpm typecheck passes
pnpm test:run passes

tasks.title: Reduce per-frame allocations
tasks.description:
Reduce GC pressure in hot paths:

1. Change tracking getters (world.ts): getAdded, getRemoved, getUpdated currently return Array.from(set) which allocates a new array each call. Change return type to ReadonlySet<number> and return the Set directly. Update the World interface in types.ts to match. Update all tests that use array matchers (toEqual([entity])) to use set-based assertions.

2. Entity iteration (entity.ts): Add a forEachEntity(callback: (entity: EntityId) => void) method to EntityManager that iterates without generator allocation. Expose it on EcsWorld and the World interface as well.

3. Query include/exclude copies (world.ts:153-154): The query method copies include and exclude arrays with [...include] and [...exclude]. These copies exist to prevent mutation of the originals. Keep these for correctness but note this is one-time per query creation, not per iteration — so it's acceptable.

Focus on items 1 and 2. Do NOT change the query result object allocation yet (that requires more API design thought around reuse semantics).

tasks.title: System phases / stages

tasks.title: Deferred command buffer
tasks.description:
Add a Commands object for deferring world mutations during system execution. This is the proper solution for iteration safety — mutations are queued during a system's execution and applied after the system finishes.

New file src/engine/ecs/commands.ts:
- Define Commands<R> interface with: createEntity() => EntityId (returns a reserved placeholder), destroyEntity(entity), addComponent(entity, type, data), removeComponent(entity, type).
- Implement CommandBuffer<R> class that records commands into an array.
- Add a flush(world) method that applies all recorded commands to the world in order, then clears the buffer.
- createEntity in the command buffer should call world.createEntity() immediately (so the returned ID is valid for subsequent addComponent commands in the same system). Alternatively, defer creation too and return a placeholder — but immediate creation is simpler and more useful.

Update src/engine/ecs/systems.ts:
- Change the System type to (world, dt, commands) => void. Keep backward compatibility: if a system function has length <= 2, don't pass commands (or always pass it — TypeScript allows extra args).
- The Scheduler creates a CommandBuffer before each system, passes it to the system, and flushes it after the system returns.

Update ecs/index.ts to export the new module.

Add tests: commands.destroyEntity during query iteration doesn't affect iteration, commands.addComponent is visible after flush, multiple commands execute in order.

tasks.title: Query caching
tasks.description:
Add persistent query handles that avoid re-evaluating which entities match on every iteration.

Changes:
1. src/engine/ecs/types.ts: Add CachedQuery<R, Include> interface extending Query<R, Include> — same iteration contract but the world manages its lifecycle.

2. src/engine/ecs/world.ts: Add createQuery<Include>(include, options?) method that returns a CachedQuery. Internally, a cached query stores its matched entity set (a Set<EntityId> or a dense array). When the cached query is iterated, it uses its cached entity set instead of scanning the smallest store. The world hooks into addComponent/removeComponent/destroyEntity to incrementally update all registered cached queries: when a component is added or removed, check if the entity now matches or unmatches each cached query and update accordingly.

Implementation approach (start simple):
- CachedQuery maintains a Set<EntityId> of matched entities
- On addComponent(entity, type): for each cached query whose include set contains type, check if entity now has ALL required components and NONE of the excluded — if yes, add to cached set
- On removeComponent(entity, type): for each cached query whose include set contains type, remove entity from cached set
- On destroyEntity: remove entity from all cached query sets
- The world keeps a list of registered cached queries

The existing query() method stays as-is (on-demand, no caching). createQuery() is the new cached alternative.

Add tests: cached query returns same results as on-demand query, cached query updates when components are added/removed, cached query updates when entities are destroyed, cached query respects exclude filters.

tasks.title: Entity relationships / parent-child hierarchy
tasks.description:
Add entity hierarchy support for scene graph relationships (transform inheritance, subtree operations).

New file src/engine/ecs/hierarchy.ts:
- Export a Hierarchy<R> class (or functions) that wraps a World<R> and manages parent-child relationships.
- API: setParent(child, parent), getParent(child): EntityId | undefined, getChildren(parent): readonly EntityId[], removeParent(child), isDescendantOf(entity, ancestor): boolean.
- Internal state: parentOf Map<EntityId, EntityId> and childrenOf Map<EntityId, EntityId[]>.
- setParent validates both entities are alive, prevents cycles (entity cannot be its own ancestor), removes from previous parent's children list if re-parenting.
- Register a destroy listener on the world: when an entity is destroyed, remove it from its parent's children list and recursively destroy all children (cascade delete). This is the standard game engine behavior — destroying a parent destroys the subtree. Provide an option or separate method to orphan children instead if needed.
- getChildren returns a readonly view (or copy) to prevent external mutation.

Alternative simpler approach: implement hierarchy as two built-in component types (Parent and Children) managed by helper functions. This integrates with the existing ECS query system (you can query for all entities with a Parent component). Choose whichever approach is cleaner.

Update ecs/index.ts to export the hierarchy module.

Add tests: set parent, get parent/children, destroy parent cascades to children, reparenting updates old and new parent, cycle prevention, orphan roots have no parent.
